results.title: Immich vs PhotoPrism: which self-hosted photo manager
results.content: Both index a library and serve it over the LAN. Immich keeps the original RAW file and shows a preview; PhotoPrism converts RAW for display.

results.title: Self-hosted photos for a family of four
results.content: We moved twenty years of photos from a cloud service to a Mac mini. Face grouping took one night for 60,000 photos.

results.title: RAW files in Immich: what is kept
results.content:
Uploads are stored as they arrive. A RAW file stays a RAW file;  the web view uses a

generated JPEG preview.

results.title: PhotoPrism and RAW: the converter settings
results.content: PhotoPrism reads RAW through a converter and keeps a sidecar JPEG for the browser. Darktable or RawTherapee can do the conversion.

results.title: Choosing a photo server: a comparison table
results.content: Immich, PhotoPrism and Nextcloud Memories side by side: mobile apps, face recognition, sharing, RAW support, hardware needs.

results.title: Backing up a self-hosted photo library
results.content: Back up the originals and the database. A library without its database loses albums, faces and descriptions.

results.title: Running a photo server on a Mac
results.content: Apple Silicon handles face recognition and video previews well; plan for disk space before anything else.

results.title: Photo apps for a home server, ranked
results.content: Our ranking after a year with each: Immich first for families, PhotoPrism first for photographers with large RAW archives.

results.title: Moving from a cloud photo service
results.content: Export takes days for a large library. Check that dates and locations survive the export before deleting anything.
